authoring_rules: Use natural contemporary English and level-appropriate vocabulary.
Target plausible Italian-learner errors rather than artificial distractors.
Do not reveal the tested grammar in school/verify titles or prompts.
Difficulty must come from form-meaning choice and transfer, not obscure vocabulary.
Every topic must support later cumulative unseen assessment without copying its verify items.

topics.outcome: Lo studente sceglie autonomamente la struttura di base corretta per identità/stato, possesso e presenza/esistenza, costruendo anche domande e negative senza trasferire direttamente la sintassi italiana.
must_master: be: affirmative, negative, inversion questions and short answers
have got/has got: possession, negatives, questions and short answers
there is/there are: singular/plural presence and absence
there is/are questions with any where appropriate
choice between be, have got and there is/are from meaning
basic contraction recognition and production
italian_transfer_risks: using have for age or temporary state
using is/are to express possession
omitting there in existential structures
using there is with plural nouns
double auxiliaries in questions such as Do you are / Do you have got
Italian-style word order in negatives/questions
exclude_for_now: have as a full lexical verb in advanced tense contrasts
recover_content: meaning-first comparison: who/what something is vs what someone possesses vs what exists in a place
compact form tables only after meaning distinction
verify_must_sample: meaning-based be vs have got vs there is/are choice

topics.outcome: Lo studente sceglie Past Simple o Past Continuous in base alla funzione narrativa: evento concluso/che avanza la sequenza, azione in corso o sfondo, e interruzione di un'azione in progresso.
must_master: completed event/sequence -> Past Simple
action in progress around a past reference point -> Past Continuous
background scene vs foreground event
interrupted action pattern without reducing the choice to when/while signal words
affirmative/negative/question form inside mixed contexts
simultaneous ongoing actions where appropriate
italian_transfer_risks: using Imperfetto mechanically as Past Continuous in every case
choosing from when/while alone
using Past Continuous for a completed sequence event
forgetting was/were or -ing
using did + past form in mixed questions/negatives
exclude_for_now: advanced stative-verb treatment beyond common high-frequency cases
recover_content: timeline/scene model with background vs event progression
contrast examples that share the same vocabulary but change viewpoint
5-6 guided choices with explanation after response

cumulative_ready_metadata.fresh_form_requirement: Cumulative fragments must use unseen narrative contexts, not verify rewrites.

topics.outcome: Lo studente interpreta e usa le principali espressioni temporali del Present Perfect in base al significato, distinguendo esperienza, risultato recente, durata e periodo non concluso senza applicare regole meccaniche di parola-segnale.
must_master: ever/never for experience
just for a recent completed event with present relevance
already/yet in level-appropriate affirmative/question/negative patterns
for/since for duration from a starting point or period
unfinished-time expressions such as today/this week where context requires Present Perfect
placement of core adverbs in the clause
interaction with Past Simple when a finished past time is explicitly supplied
italian_transfer_risks: using Present Perfect with yesterday/last year/ago
confusing for and since
placing yet/already/just mechanically in Italian order
treating every today/this week sentence as Present Perfect regardless of meaning
using been/gone interchangeably if the curriculum example requires the distinction
exclude_for_now: complex been vs gone taxonomy beyond core use
recover_content: meaning groups rather than a signal-word list
explicit finished-time contrast with Past Simple

topics.outcome: Lo studente sceglie e produce Zero o First Conditional in base al significato: regola/risultato generalmente vero rispetto a una condizione futura reale o probabile, mantenendo il controllo della forma verbale nelle due proposizioni.
must_master: zero conditional for general truths, routines and predictable repeated results
first conditional for real/possible future condition and consequence
present form in the if-clause rather than will
will + base form in the main clause for the canonical first-conditional target
clause order and punctuation
meaning choice between zero and first conditional from context
italian_transfer_risks: using will in the if-clause
using future forms in both clauses
choosing zero vs first solely from the word if
confusing general rule with one future possibility
wrong third-person -s or base-form control inside the condition
exclude_for_now: unless/provided/as long as except where explicitly required by a school programme
modal alternatives in the result clause as core teaching target
recover_content: meaning contrast: every time/general consequence vs one realistic future possibility
same-situation paired examples showing how meaning changes

cumulative_ready_metadata.fresh_form_requirement: Cumulative evidence must hide the conditional label and require meaning-based choice.
